lines: Fever and progressively worsening pain, redness, and swelling of right lower leg following beach vacation and foot injury 5 days ago

This 50-year-old female with chronic venous insufficiency and varicose veins, previously evaluated for bilateral lower extremity swelling in 2020 and 2021, presents to the emergency department with acute lower leg symptoms.
She returned from a family beach vacation 5 days ago and recalls stepping on something sharp while walking barefoot in the sand, but she did not initially notice any injury.
Over the past 2 days, she has developed progressively worsening pain and swelling of her lower leg, which is now interfering with her ability to walk.
She reports chills and feels generally unwell.
